summary.text: A heat engine is a system that uses heat moving from a hot source to a cold sink to do mechanical or electrical work.
Only part of the heat becomes work; some escapes to the surroundings and some is wasted on friction and drag.
Carnot's theorem caps how efficient any heat engine can be, but nearly any energy source can be turned into heat, so these engines are used almost everywhere.

facts.label: Working substance
facts.value: Usually a gas or a liquid

facts.label: Cold side on Earth
facts.value: Stuck near ambient temperature, about 300 kelvin

facts.label: Run in reverse
facts.value: Refrigerators, air conditioners and heat pumps

facts.label: Natural example
facts.value: A Hadley cell in Earth's atmosphere

items.prompt: A car is cruising along fine, yet its exhaust pipe and engine block are very hot. What does that heat mostly represent?

options.label: Energy that never entered the engine at all
Heat that was not turned into work and was lost
A sign that the engine is about to break down
Work that the engine is saving for later use

items.explain: Some heat is normally lost to the surroundings and is not converted to work.

items.prompt: Two engines use the same kind of design and both dump heat to ordinary room-temperature air. One burns at a much higher temperature. Which has the higher potential efficiency?

options.label: The one with the hotter source
The one with the cooler source
Neither; the cold side alone decides it
Both equal, since the air is the same

items.explain: The larger the temperature gap between hot source and cold sink, the larger the potential efficiency. The cold side is stuck near ambient, so a hotter source widens the gap.

items.prompt: The back of a kitchen fridge feels warm while its inside is cold. What is going on?

options.label: The motor makes heat that has nothing to do with cooling
Cold air is being converted into warm air in the walls
Work is used to move heat from inside out to the room
The insulation slowly turns food energy into heat

items.explain: A refrigerator is a heat engine run in reverse: it uses work to take heat from the cold chamber and vent it at a higher temperature to the environment.

items.prompt: One engine runs on burning coal, another on a nuclear reactor, another on concentrated sunlight. Why can the same kind of machine use such different fuels?

options.label: Each fuel secretly makes the same kind of fuel gas
The machine changes shape to suit each energy source
Only the hot gas matters, and every source adds the same chemicals
All these sources can be turned into heat, which is all it needs

items.explain: The heat source can be powered by virtually any kind of energy, since most energy forms are easily converted to heat.

items.prompt: An engineer says: a diesel engine is a machine, while the Diesel cycle is something else. What is the cycle?

options.label: An idealised model that the real machine tries to follow
The part of the machine that carries the fuel
A name for how long the engine has been running
The exact record of what every real engine does

items.explain: The word engine is used for the physical device and cycle for the model, and few real engines match their cycles exactly.

items.prompt: Warm moist air rises near the equator and cooler air sinks farther north and south, driving a steady circulation. Why do physicists call this a heat engine?

options.label: It burns fuel in the upper atmosphere
It stores sunlight inside the clouds for later
It makes electricity directly from the wind
Heat flow makes the air move, producing kinetic energy

items.explain: A Hadley cell is a thermally driven circulation with a net production of kinetic energy, so heat flowing from warm to cold does work.
